posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
So, after I did quite a lot of battleback conversions and I talked a lot how I never upscale Ace tiles with a scaling algorithm but manually to keep them crisp and pretty, I though I might lay my hands on some of the tiles and make them ready for plug and play use without any quality loss. I honestly don't know how extensive this will be, I guess that will depend on my mood and how excited you guys are about the results ;3

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Well, it's not like you have any other choice than waiting patiently ;P
One of the interesting things of this projects is that I basically have to think out of the box all the time and see how I can make things doable in a reasonable time. Because: Sure, technically I am able to upscale and repixel the tiles, but that would not make sense in any way.
For example:
I could upscale and repixel it. OR....
I use those two bits that I already made and only do the white vase and make it an edit that resembles the tile instead!
The vase I then manually repixeled:
And edited my jars to be smaller, assembled everything and put a shadow below them:
So you see, depending on the tile, there are quite some hoops I am jumping through, depending on what I am doing. But that is still way faster than doing it by upscaling and reworking the whole thing.
And just for a good measure: the Ace RTP contains 4560 tiles. Quite some are used on multiple sheets, but that means I have to find hundreds of different solutions for different cases ;3
There are quite some cases where I don't see that solution yet, but that is also why this is so all over the place: I am chipping away at the ones I see a way to do them and therefore slowly but surely make my progress. Or not so slowly tbh.

And here is the final release.
You can find all the complete sheets in the start post now as well.
Why is it that I always post here when I am super tired? Or am I just always tired lately? Who knows?
But I can really use some feedback on this whole project, it was really insane to say the least.
We close with my arch enemies, those goddam motherfreaking waterlilies and crates with weapons.
But I managed to convert everything. Which means either I am an unmatched master of upscaling or that everything is actually upscalable without much quality loss if you are patient and resourceful.
Now in the end I am a bit annoyed that I didn't keep wips cause I think a tutorial might have been useful for those who want to tackle certain things from packs or user threads... oh well...
I can really use some uplifting words that make this madness worthwile, and besides that, well, it is 100% done and released.
Bit annoyed that it ends on a double post though, but seems like I would have had to wait forever for anyone to say something.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
It's really great that you've finished this huge job.  Congratulations, and thanks for your generosity in doing it.
It's incredibly difficult to pick out what are my favourites, and anyway, that will probably change depending on what I need, but especially honourable mention goes to the following:
Dungeon C: the rail tracks.  Those have to be exactly the right size to tile together, so getting them in 48x48 already saves so much time.  Big bonus is that they are not the horrible colour of the MZ version, and are much easier to recolour if I want to e.g. darken the wood to match other wood pieces.
Inside B: The fireplaces.  I don't want a metal flue on a brick fireplace (MZ), so great that I don't have to!  The broken window panes on the same tile sheet are a must-have.  I bet they were fiddly to do.
Outside B:  I've already mentioned the snowy scarecrow and the superb little icicles hanging from its hat.  The same goes for the tiny icicles on the snowy log, especially the ones around the edge of the hollow interior.  Brilliant piece of work.
World B:  The ruined towers with window slots.
An eccentric choice, I admit.  But the whole set is such a high standard that literally anything would be worthy of mention.
Once again, many thanks.
